# Digital Adoption Platforms (DAPs): The Software Alternative to Human Adoption Consultants

## The Category Story (2026)

DAPs sell one core promise: instead of paying human trainers/consultants to teach people software, you overlay a **software guidance layer** on top of any application that walks users through it in-app. The universal narrative beats are: *don't send people to training → guide them inside the tool, at the moment of need → measure adoption → prove ROI.*

A key **2026 shift** frames the competitive story: the category is moving from **rule-based, pre-scripted overlays** (a human builds every tooltip/flow in advance, same for everyone) toward **AI-inferred, behavioral guidance** (the system detects when a user is stuck from real-time signals and reaches users "who never ask"). This is the exact fault line your topic cares about — guidance tied to the *software* (any user hitting a screen) vs. guidance adapted to the *individual person*.

**Crucial structural point for your framing:** almost every DAP guides based on **where the user is in the software** (which screen, which field, which role-segment), *not* on who the person is as an individual with their own goals and history. The guidance lives on the app, not on the person. Even the "personalized" claims are mostly **role/segment-based** (e.g. "show sales this flow, show HR that one"), not a persistent per-person agent. That is the gap.

---

## 1. WalkMe — the enterprise-IT incumbent
**What it is:** The original enterprise DAP; a guidance/automation layer overlaid on enterprise apps (SAP, Salesforce, Workday, ServiceNow, Dynamics). Acquired by SAP.
**URL:** https://www.walkme.com/

**Verbatim hero:** *"WalkMe turns AI potential into AI performance."*
**Subhead:** *"WalkMe is the critical layer that makes enterprise AI work."*
**In-app guidance story:** Guides users through workflows *"inside the tools they already use. No training class. No help desk ticket."* Older category copy: on-screen *"Walk-Thrus — dynamic step-by-step instructions,"* a *"guidance layer added on top of any existing website, software or online platform."* It *"overlays on any application, identifies where critical workflows break, and then provides personalized guidance and automation."*
**Angle:** Kill training classes and help-desk tickets; prove AI/software ROI to the enterprise.
**Who they talk to:** **Enterprise IT / transformation leaders**, plus dept heads (Sales, HR, Customer Care). Buyer is the org rolling out software to employees.
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software.** The overlay sits on the application and fires by screen/workflow break. "Personalized" = role/context within the workflow, not a per-person agent.

---

## 2. Whatfix — the "in-app guidance" purebred
**What it is:** Enterprise DAP with the most literal "in-app guidance" positioning; strong L&D/change-management tilt.
**URL:** https://whatfix.com/

**Verbatim hero:** *"Increase user adoption with in-app guidance."*
**Subhead:** *"In-app guidance. Hands-on simulations. Actionable analytics. One unified platform to drive adoption and maximize ROI."*
**In-app guidance story:** Contextual *"Flows, Smart Tips, Pop-Ups, and Task Lists to standardize task execution and enable faster onboarding"* across web, desktop, mobile. Category line: *"empower anyone, anywhere to have scalable success with technology they use every day."*
**Angle:** Replace one-time training with continuous, contextual, in-flow help; scale change management.
**Who they talk to:** **L&D and HR** first, then Sales and Product; regulated industries (banking, healthcare, insurance, pharma, public sector). 700+ orgs.
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software**, with role/segment personalization. Flows are authored on the app screens; users get them by role/segment, not as individuals.

---

## 3. Pendo — analytics-first, adoption-second
**What it is:** Product-analytics platform that bundles in-app guides; positions adoption as the outcome of understanding behavior.
**URL:** https://www.pendo.io/

**Verbatim hero:** *"Close the gap between AI spend and AI adoption."*
**Subhead:** *"Pendo captures user behavior across your software and agents, identifies where users struggle, and puts that context to work—so your AI gets smarter in real time and every user gets a better experience."*
**In-app guides copy:** *"Help users right where they need it."* Guides *"speed up onboarding and adoption with relevant, contextual in-app messages"*; with *"conditional logic built into your guides, you can deliver tailored content and next steps that match individual needs."* AI authoring via *"Leo, Pendo's conversational interface."*
**Angle:** Data → insight → guided action. "Know what users love, where they struggle, what they ignore. Guide them to value."
**Who they talk to:** **Product teams** primarily, plus IT/enterprise deploying software and AI agents.
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software + behavior.** Closest to "individual" via conditional logic that adapts steps to a user's choices — but still triggered by in-product behavior on the app, not a standing personal agent that knows the human across contexts.

---

## 4. Userlane — regulated-industry, "put people at the heart"
**What it is:** Software adoption platform aimed squarely at regulated enterprises; leans on a human/people framing.
**URL:** https://www.userlane.com/

**Verbatim hero:** *"Remove Friction / Reduce Cost / Improve Adoption"*
**Subhead:** *"The intelligence to see the impact of your software and AI. The assistance to help your people get work done."*
**In-app guidance story:** Help *"directly within applications through contextual assistance — including AI-powered answers, structured workflow guidance, and automated processes — rather than relying on separate training sessions that users forget quickly."* Solution page: *"Software adoption, made easy"*; guidance *"from first click to full adoption."* Campaign line: *"Put people at the heart of digital transformation."*
**Angle:** Training you forget vs. real-time in-workflow support; ROI justification for expensive implementations.
**Who they talk to:** **Enterprise IT / ops in regulated industries** (healthcare, manufacturing, financial services, insurance, energy, public sector).
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software.** Despite the "people at the heart" language, guidance is workflow/role-structured on the app; "people" is the emotional frame, not per-individual personalization.

---

## 5. Userpilot — PLG / product-growth, no-code
**What it is:** Product-growth platform for SaaS teams; in-app onboarding + analytics + monetization.
**URL:** https://userpilot.com/

**Verbatim hero:** *"Product Analytics and Onboarding Platform for User Monetization."*
**Subhead:** *"Userpilot helps product and growth teams turn user signals into activation, adoption, retention, and revenue."*
**In-app guidance story:** Build *"in-app onboarding flows without code"* with *"tooltips, banners, spotlights, and contextual nudges"*; *"launch, iterate, and optimize without a single dev ticket."* 2026 addition: *"Lia: the only platform in this category with a project-based AI agent that automates the full insight-to-action loop."*
**Angle:** Ship growth experiences without engineering; guide users to value → revenue.
**Who they talk to:** **Product management, growth, PMM, UX, CS** at ~1,200+ SaaS companies. Buyer is the **software vendor**, guiding *their own customers*.
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software**, segment-personalized. The AI ("Lia") automates building flows, not being a personal companion to each end-user.

---

## 6. Appcues — onboarding-first, human/emotional voice
**What it is:** Product-led onboarding and adoption tool; warmest, most human brand voice in the set.
**URL:** https://www.appcues.com/

**Verbatim hero:** *"Build experiences that move people."*
**Subhead:** *"Meet customers at every stage with a platform built to drive outcomes."*
**Other real copy:** *"Adoption is where attention becomes habit."* Helps customers *"find their footing, hit their first wins, and keep coming back"*; *"turn first wins into routines users return to"* and *"move customers from one feature to many."* No-code: build/test/publish *"without waiting on engineering."*
**Angle:** Emotional/habit framing — attention → habit, first win → routine. Onboarding as the relationship's opening move.
**Who they talk to:** **Product, growth, and CS teams** at SaaS companies guiding their own users.
**Guidance tied to software or person?** **Software**, segment-driven ("personalized, segment-driven messaging delivered at critical moments"). Personalization = segment + lifecycle stage, not per-individual identity.

---

## 7. The AI-native shift (Whatfix AI, Apty, and the 2026 framing)
Rather than one clean new logo, the newer story is **AI-native repositioning** across the field, articulated most sharply by analysts and challengers:
- The contrast copy: *"Generic walkthroughs and static help content treat all users the same, leading to irrelevant guidance."*
- The new claim: *"An AI-powered adoption platform infers when a user needs help from real-time behavioral signals, including situations no one scripted for, and reaches users who never ask"* — versus *"a rule-based DAP [that] fires guidance based on rules a human configured in advance."*
- Aspirational personalization: *"guidance adapts to an individual user's role, skill level, and current workflow."*

**Sources:** https://userpilot.com/blog/digital-adoption-platforms/ , https://apty.ai/blog/best-digital-adoption-platforms/ , https://whatfix.com/blog/ai-in-digital-adoption-programs/

---

## The Contrast That Matters For Your Narrative

| Player | Hero framing | In-app guidance form | Primary buyer | Tied to… |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WalkMe | "AI potential into AI performance" | Walk-Thrus overlaid on enterprise apps | Enterprise IT | **Software** |
| Whatfix | "Increase adoption with in-app guidance" | Flows, Smart Tips, Task Lists | L&D / HR | **Software** (role) |
| Pendo | "Close the gap between AI spend and adoption" | Behavior-triggered guides + conditional logic | Product | **Software + behavior** |
| Userlane | "Put people at the heart" | Contextual workflow guidance | Regulated-IT | **Software** |
| Userpilot | "…Platform for User Monetization" | No-code tooltips/nudges | SaaS product/growth | **Software** (segment) |
| Appcues | "Build experiences that move people" | Segment-driven onboarding flows | SaaS product/CS | **Software** (segment) |
| AI-native 2026 | "Reaches users who never ask" | Behavioral, inferred guidance | Enterprise + product | **Software behavior** (aspiring to person) |

**The load-bearing insight:** every one of these guides the user relative to **the software** — the screen they're on, the workflow step, at best their *role/segment*. Even the AI-native pitch personalizes by *behavior signals inside the app*, not by a durable model of the *individual person* that follows them across everything they do. The guidance is a layer on the **product**; nobody in this category owns a layer on the **person**. Whoever attaches step-by-step guidance to the *human* (their goals, history, cross-app life) rather than to *a piece of software* is telling a story the whole DAP category structurally cannot.

**All sources:** [WalkMe](https://www.walkme.com/) · [Whatfix](https://whatfix.com/) · [Pendo](https://www.pendo.io/) · [Pendo in-app guides](https://www.pendo.io/product/in-app-guides/) · [Userlane](https://www.userlane.com/) · [Userlane in-app guidance 2026](https://www.userlane.com/blog/the-state-of-in-app-guidance-2026/) · [Userpilot](https://userpilot.com/) · [Appcues](https://www.appcues.com/) · [Appcues onboarding use case](https://www.appcues.com/use-case/onboarding) · [Userpilot DAP 2026](https://userpilot.com/blog/digital-adoption-platforms/) · [Apty best DAPs](https://apty.ai/blog/best-digital-adoption-platforms/) · [Whatfix AI in adoption](https://whatfix.com/blog/ai-in-digital-adoption-programs/)

# Adoption Doesn't End at Launch: Players Owning the "Hypercare / Sustained Adoption / Beyond Go-Live" Narrative

Research date: July 2026. All quotes below are verbatim from the cited pages. Quotes marked **[fetched]** were pulled directly from the live page; quotes marked **[search-snippet]** come from search-result excerpts and could not be re-verified because the page blocked direct fetch (flagged for transparency).

---

## 1. Whatfix — Digital Adoption Platform (DAP)
**What it is:** In-app guidance/DAP vendor. URL: https://whatfix.com/blog/hypercare-support/

**Narrative — verbatim [fetched]:**
- "Post-go-live hypercare is the period of heightened support and stabilization following a new application launch"
- "The purpose of hypercare is to keep critical workflows moving while users adjust to the new system"
- "After go-live, the challenge shifts from rolling out a new system to stabilizing how people use it in live work"
- "Hypercare should end when support demand is stable enough for business-as-usual teams to own the remaining work"

**Frame / angle:** Operational-support framing. Launch is a *transition point, not completion*. Story arc: post-launch ticket spike → workflow friction as root cause → structured hypercare (daily triage, escalation, deflection) → stabilization metrics. Positions the DAP as the infrastructure that carries adoption past go-live.

**Who they talk to:** Service desk teams, ITSM process owners, enterprise application owners, access/security teams. Technical/operational buyer.

---

## 2. Panorama Consulting Group — Independent ERP Consultancy
**What it is:** Vendor-independent ERP implementation/advisory firm. URL: https://www.panorama-consulting.com/erp-hypercare-checklist/

**Narrative — verbatim [fetched]:**
- "ERP hypercare is the structured stabilization period that follows go-live."
- "Hypercare should be treated as a business stabilization effort rather than a temporary support queue."
- "A strong ERP hypercare plan reinforces user adoption by helping employees apply new processes consistently under real operating conditions."
- "Many early post-go-live issues are rooted in user behavior and process execution rather than in the software itself."

**Frame / angle:** Hypercare as *business-critical risk management*, not IT support. Executives should drive priorities by operational impact, not vendor/IT pressure. Emotional pull: fear of a costly post-go-live failure, answered with governance and accountability.

**Who they talk to:** Finance leaders, operations executives, IT directors owning ERP implementations.

---

## 3. IMA Worldwide — Organizational Change Management (OCM) Firm
**What it is:** Change management consultancy. URL: https://imaworldwide.com/why-change-fails-after-go-live-sustaining-adoption-beyond-launch/

**Narrative — verbatim [fetched]:**
- "Go-live is not the finish line. What comes after go-live is just as important: ongoing support, user adoption monitoring, and continuous improvement."
- "Indeed, the go-live phase is not merely a conclusion but the critical starting point for an ongoing commitment to system efficacy and sustained adoption."
- "From go-live onward, success depends on how people incorporate the change into their daily work. This is where things get difficult."
- "The real issue is how organizations respond. If this phase is ignored or minimized: frustration increases, confidence drops, workarounds become permanent."

**Frame / angle:** Go-live as *a beginning, not an ending*. Emotional stakes are explicit — frustration, dropping confidence, permanent workarounds, reversion to old habits. Success is measured by behavior change months after launch, not by deployment.

**Who they talk to:** Organizational leaders, change practitioners, enterprise teams facing post-implementation drift.

---

## 4. Assima — Digital Adoption Platform / Training
**What it is:** DAP and enterprise training vendor. URL: https://assimasolutions.com/resources/blog/training-beyond-go-live-dap-features/

**Narrative — verbatim [fetched]:**
- "Training cannot be treated as a one-time event; it must extend into daily workflows."
- "Long-term software adoption requires organizations to think beyond training sessions and user manuals."
- "Employees don't retain information unless they use it consistently."

**Frame / angle:** Reframes training from a pre-launch event into an ongoing, in-workflow requirement. Leans on the forgetting curve (≈70% of new info lost within 24 hours) and productivity/error spikes to make continuous in-app guidance "business-critical" rather than nice-to-have. Positions DAPs as the mechanism for sustained adoption and ROI.

**Who they talk to:** L&D professionals, IT leaders, enterprise change teams rolling out SAP, Oracle, Salesforce.

---

## 5. OTT, Inc. — ERP Implementation Partner

# The "Parachute In, Drive Adoption, Then Leave" Consulting Narrative
## Market/Narrative Research — Who Owns "We Make Ourselves Obsolete"

**Bottom line:** Yes, this narrative is actively owned — but it's fragmented. The change-management and adoption-consulting space has largely converged on a shared vocabulary ("capability transfer," "self-sufficient," "sustainable adoption," "no dependency"). What almost nobody does is turn it into a sharp, emotional, brand-defining *promise*. The strongest single articulation I found is a 2025 Avencia thought-leadership piece, not a positioning line on a big firm's homepage. That's the opening: the frame exists as industry jargon, but no dominant player has claimed "we don't want to be here forever" as its identity.

---

## The Players

### 1. Avencia Consulting — the sharpest verbatim articulation of the whole frame
- **What it is:** UK recruitment/talent + consulting firm. The relevant asset is a thought-leadership article, *"Capability is the real legacy of consultancy"* (30 Oct 2025).
- **URL:** https://www.avenciaconsulting.com/capability-is-the-real-legacy-of-consultancy/
- **NARRATIVE (verbatim):**
  - *"The real legacy of consultancy should be capability."*
  - *"Too many consultancies operate on a dependency model. They deliver the project, issue the final invoice, and leave."*
  - *"The best consultancies measure success by what clients can do after they leave. The worst measure success by how long they can stay."*
  - *"Capability means knowledge transfer. It means embedding playbooks, templates, and habits that internal teams can use long after the consultants are gone."*
  - *"If a consultancy engagement ends and the client feels weaker, not stronger, something has gone wrong."*
- **Frame & emotional angle:** This is the clearest "we make ourselves obsolete" argument in the set. It explicitly *attacks* the dependency model as the enemy and reframes leaving as the proof of value. The "feels weaker, not stronger" line is the emotional hook.

- **Frame & emotional angle:** "Install vs. implement" gap. The pitch is that most consulting *installs* and leaves, whereas they build the internal muscle so *your own people run it*. Less confrontational than Avencia, more methodology-as-legacy.

## Cross-Cutting Observations (the narrative white space)

1. **The vocabulary is shared and generic.** "Capability transfer," "self-sufficient," "sustainable adoption," "no dependency," "embed and exit," "make change stick" recur across nearly every firm. It has become table-stakes jargon, which means it *doesn't differentiate anyone.*

2. **Almost nobody makes it emotional or identity-level.** The frame lives as a bullet point ("capability transfer over consultant dependency") rather than a brand promise. The one exception is Avencia's article — and it's thought leadership, not their core positioning.

3. **The strongest structural claim is Changefirst's** (license the method, prove it with a 40%-cost-reduction stat). Proof-by-numbers ("we made ourselves 40% less necessary") is far more credible than adjectives.

4. **"We make ourselves obsolete" as an owned, front-and-center identity is unclaimed.** No player builds its whole brand around *"we don't want to be here forever."* Clerestory names a method "EMBED," IMA says "sticks not installs," Avencia writes the manifesto — but no one has planted a flag on the emotional promise itself. # The Adoption & Change-Agent Narrative Landscape
### Market/narrative research, July 2026. Verbatim copy from live vendor pages; unverified quotes flagged inline.

## 1. System-Implementation Partners — how SIs frame ADOPTION vs. the technical build

The industry has converged on one thesis: **"technology implementation is really a people transformation."** The build is treated as commoditized; adoption/change is where value is won or lost. Every player pairs a soft human story with a hard ROI stat.

**Accenture** — Change Management practice. https://www.accenture.com/us-en/services/talent-organization/change-management
- *"People at the heart of change."*
- *"Create a vision of the future… where they feel change is happening with them, not to them."*
- *"Continuous change is the new reality. Leaders can see the pressing need for change but lack the confidence to deliver."*
- Frame: change as a permanent, accelerating condition. Angle: empowerment/inclusion ("with them, not to them"). Audience: C-suite/CHRO.

**Deloitte** — OCM / SAP & Workday alliance. https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/alliances/articles/workday-erp-change-management-adoption.html
- *"Technology implementations are, at their core, people transformations."*
- *"ERP change management is a journey, not a destination."*
- *"Empathy is a practical differentiator. Some users will welcome a new system; others will worry about capability, workload or job security."*
- *"A 134% ROI can be achieved when 'excellent' change programs are part of the SAP S/4HANA transformation."*
- Frame: "implementation activity" vs. "durable transformation." Angle: empathy + named user fear, validated by ROI. Audience: enterprise execs.

**PwC** — NextGen Change. https://www.pwc.com/us/en/services/consulting/business-transformation/workforce-transformation/nextgen-change.html *(page 403 — quotes are search-snippet, not page-verified)*
- *"A human-centered approach that moves beyond traditional change management"* — pillars: *"Leader & Citizen Activation, Personalized Experiences, Essential Skills & Behaviors."*
- Frame: positions *against* "traditional change management"; "citizen activation" = employees as participants. Audience: CHRO.

**Capgemini** — Enablement as a Service. https://www.capgemini.com/solutions/enablement-as-a-service/
- *"Are you supporting your employees with standard training? Or empowering them in real-time with EaaS-ier enablement?"*
- *"The key to successful technology-driven change at work lies in treating employees as customers…"*
- Frame: episodic training → always-on enablement, productized "as a Service." Angle: consumer-grade employee experience. Audience: SAP transformation owners.

**Infosys** — Enterprise Change Consulting. https://www.infosys.com/services/consulting/offerings/enterprise-change.html *(403 — search-snippet)*
- *"Human issues remain the primary barrier to success in transformation programs."* / *"drive adoption at scale"* with *"350 global practitioners."*
- Frame: people as the risk; industrialized scale. Angle: rational/risk-mitigation. Audience: CIO/program sponsor.

**Cognizant** — packaged Microsoft 365 Copilot "Adoption and Change Management" SKU. https://appsource.microsoft.com/en-us/marketplace/consulting-services/cognizant.adoption_and_change_management *(search-snippet)*

## 2. The Transient Change-Agent Model — "we parachute in, then leave"

**The narrative exists as shared jargon ("capability transfer," "self-sufficient," "embed and exit") but almost nobody owns it as an emotional, brand-defining promise.** The strongest single articulation is a thought-leadership article, not a homepage.

**Avencia** — *"Capability is the real legacy of consultancy"* (Oct 2025). https://www.avenciaconsulting.com/capability-is-the-real-legacy-of-consultancy/
- *"Too many consultancies operate on a dependency model. They deliver the project, issue the final invoice, and leave."*
- *"The best consultancies measure success by what clients can do after they leave. The worst measure success by how long they can stay."*
- *"If a consultancy engagement ends and the client feels weaker, not stronger, something has gone wrong."*
- The clearest "we make ourselves obsolete" manifesto in the set — but it's an article, not their positioning.

**IMA Worldwide** (AIM methodology). https://imaworldwide.com/change-management-consulting-aim/
- *"Organizational change management consulting that sticks. Not just installs."*
- *"Capability transfer over consultant dependency."* / *"Build an enterprise change capability your own people run."*

**Changefirst** (PCI® method, licensed SaaS). https://www.changefirst.com/business-issues/build-ecm-capability
- *"make change everyone's business"*; *"a sustainable enterprise-level change capability."* Proof: Syngenta *"drove capability costs down by 40% over 3 years"* — the most *structural* commitment to obsolescence (license the method vs. staff-aug).

**Prosci** — productized capability transfer via train-the-trainer certification (*self-sufficient rather than long-term dependency* — search-reported, advisory page 403). **Clerestory Consulting** — trademarked **EMBED℠** method, the closest anyone comes to naming "embed and exit" (page 502, unverified). **Daggerwing** — *"how people actually adopt, embrace, and sustain transformation"* (https://daggerwinggroup.com/); self-sufficiency present but soft.

**White space:** the vocabulary is generic and undifferentiating. No player builds its identity around *"we don't want to be here forever."* That lane is open.

## 3. Digital Adoption Platforms — the software alternative to consultants

DAPs overlay an in-app guidance layer on any software and walk users through it. **Structurally, every DAP guides the user relative to the SOFTWARE — the screen, the workflow step, at best their role/segment — never as a persistent per-person companion.**

**WalkMe** (SAP), enterprise-IT incumbent. https://www.walkme.com/ — *"WalkMe turns AI potential into AI performance."* / *"the critical layer that makes enterprise AI work"*; guidance *"inside the tools they already use. No training class. No help desk ticket."* Tied to: **software**.

**Whatfix** — the "in-app guidance" purebred. https://whatfix.com/ — *"Increase user adoption with in-app guidance."* / *"Flows, Smart Tips, Pop-Ups, and Task Lists."* Audience: L&D/HR. Tied to: **software (role/segment)**.

**Pendo** — analytics-first. https://www.pendo.io/ — *"Close the gap between AI spend and AI adoption."* *"Help users right where they need it"*; *"conditional logic… deliver tailored content and next steps that match individual needs."* The closest to individual, but still triggered by in-product behavior. Tied to: **software + behavior**.

**Userlane** — regulated industries. https://www.userlane.com/ — *"Put people at the heart of digital transformation"*; help *"directly within applications… rather than relying on separate training sessions that users forget."* "People" is the frame, not per-individual personalization. Tied to: **software**.

**Userpilot** (https://userpilot.com/ — *"…Platform for User Monetization"*) and **Appcues** (https://www.appcues.com/ — *"Build experiences that move people"* / *"Adoption is where attention becomes habit"*) — PLG tools where the *software vendor* guides *their own customers*, segment-personalized.

**2026 AI-native shift:** the challenger contrast — *"Generic walkthroughs and static help content treat all users the same, leading to irrelevant guidance,"* vs. AI that *"infers when a user needs help from real-time behavioral signals… and reaches users who never ask"* (userpilot.com/blog, whatfix.com/blog/ai-in-digital-adoption-programs/). Even this personalizes by *behavior signals inside the app*, not a durable model of the individual.

## 4. Hypercare / Sustained Adoption — "adoption is not a one-time event"

Universal hook: **"Go-live is not the finish line."** Two vocabularies: consultancies say **"hypercare"** (bounded 30–90 day stabilization); OCM/DAP say **"sustainment / continuous adoption"** (open-ended). Shared villain: users reverting to old habits, workarounds becoming permanent.

- **Whatfix** (https://whatfix.com/blog/hypercare-support/): *"After go-live, the challenge shifts from rolling out a new system to stabilizing how people use it in live work."*

## The Gap — does anyone tell the story of a PERSONAL, PERSISTENT companion for the INDIVIDUAL employee?

**No. The market splits three ways, and all three miss the individual-person axis:**

1. **Consultants** serve the **organization**, temporarily. Their entire narrative — even the "we leave you self-sufficient" strand — is about transferring capability to *the org's internal team*, then exiting. The employee is a segment to be moved, not a person to be accompanied.
2. **DAPs** attach guidance to the **software**, permanently but impersonally. Every walkthrough is anchored to a screen/workflow/role. Even AI-native DAPs personalize by *behavior inside the app*, not by a durable model of the human across their whole work life. The layer sits on the *product*, never on the *person*.
3. **Hypercare/sustainment** players correctly say adoption is ongoing and behavioral — but their "ongoing" support is still an org-level program or an in-app layer, not a one-to-one presence that knows *this individual*.

**The unclaimed narrative:** a **personal, persistent companion that walks the individual employee through the change one-on-one** — tied to the *person* (their goals, history, cross-app life), not to the org (a consultant who leaves) or the software (a generic tooltip that treats all users the same). Three phrases the incumbents have left on the table and that map exactly to this positioning:
- The consultants' honest promise, made permanent instead of transient: *"we leave you stronger, not weaker"* — except it never leaves.
- The DAPs' structural blind spot: they guide by screen; **nobody guides by person.**
- The hypercare truth taken to its logical end: if *"adoption is not a one-time event,"* the only thing that can sustain it forever is something that stays with the individual forever — which a consultant (by design temporary) and a tooltip (by design impersonal) cannot be.
